canonical_statement: If a first-order sentence in a left language semantically entails a sentence in a right language, then there is an interpolating sentence using only their common language which is entailed by the left sentence and entails the right sentence.
domain_and_universes: FirstOrder.Language.{u,v}; sentences and structures in the associated mathlib universes; Prop
quantifiers: P : CraigInterpolationProblem Lcommon Lleft Lright Ltotal
hypotheses: language maps embed the common language into both sides and both sides into a joint language
the two common-to-joint language maps commute
the embedded left sentence semantically entails the embedded right sentence in the empty joint theory
conclusion: There exists a common-language sentence theta such that the left sentence entails its left translation and its right translation entails the right sentence.

alternate_encodings.target: single ambient signature with symbol-support intersection
alternate_encodings.relationship: expected equivalent after explicit language-reduct/support transports

excluded_degenerate_cases: No equality or disjointness of the side languages is assumed. Empty common languages and identical side languages remain included. Theory-relative, infinitary, propositional, and higher-order interpolation are outside this root.
